complexity_ledger.narrative: CD-02 writes the complexity intuition: references/complexity_intuition.md, a doc an agent reads ALONGSIDE an `analyze complexity` descriptor to decide whether and how to refactor. It covers: the "how complex should a program be" best practice (complexity proportional to essential behavior; a validated refactor that lowers complexity -- TLC/tests green, behavior preserved, before/after descriptors compared -- is encouraged as normal practice, not an exceptional event); what good and bad descriptor shapes look like, section by section of the real output; five worked examples, every excerpt verbatim scanner output from real runs (a modular two-subsystem model with Q=0.314 and one port-crossing action; a pipeline showing Q=0.000 on a clean single-writer design; a god-state model with oversized domains, unconstrained variables and a TLC run that did not finish in 120s; the validated before/after refactor of that model, bound 1,654,784 -> 576 with TLC going from timeout to green 36 distinct states; and this repository's own program_model descriptor as the mixed real-world case, including the deliberate lastCommand/result observability unknowns and the max_distinct_states 500000 budget rationale); and a reading order for forming a refactor recommendation. Everywhere explicit: intuitions for the agent to judge with, never automated moves -- CD-01 removed the suggested-move output because it was confidently wrong, and this doc makes no automated-suggestion claims on the scanner's behalf. SKILL.md wires the refactor-input framing into the shipped-descriptor paragraph, the "Complexity Budgets Are Advisory" doctrine, and the References index. Retention oracles (kill_rate/effect_conformance/external_coverage) were not re-run: the model is byte-identical to the CD-01 baseline, behavior retention is witnessed by the identical TLC run, and no complexity decrease is claimed that would require them. Per the epic's case_execution_rule the fuzzing machinery is experimental and not ticket validation. One out-of-scope defect deferred (batch mode): CD-02-DF-01, the misleading "no readable spec manifest at does-not-exist" warning path emitted from scripts/analyze_complexity.py:1044 when no --manifest is supplied.

The TLA+ model, configs, manifest, adapters and tests are byte-identical to the epic baseline merged by CD-01 (ticket current/ == desired/, verified by diff -r), and TLC reports the same figures as CD-01: 5,619,356 states generated / 231,621 distinct / depth 25 (results/tlc_current.txt), 46.3% of the negotiated max_distinct_states 500000 carried through desired/spec_manifest.yaml with its rationale. The refinement search for an architectural reduction found none applicable: the ticket's objective is to teach descriptor reading, not to change the model. The doc's before/after worked example was produced on external scratch models, not on this program's model.

ticket.objective: Write references/complexity_intuition.md: guidance an agent reads ALONGSIDE a CD-01 descriptor to decide whether and how to refactor — NOT automated suggestions (CD-01 removed those because they were wrong). Teach what a GOOD descriptor looks like (bound proportional to essential behavior, high modularity / clean clusters, balanced R/W matrix, no god-state, domains sized to the real distinctions) and what a BAD one looks like (god-state / dense rows, low modularity, bound exploding past the behavior, domains wider than the behavior needs), with concrete worked good/bad examples and reasoning. Wire the framing "take this complexity descriptor to consider how to refactor complexity out of the app" into the workflow/doctrine. OWNER ADDENDUM (2026-07-21): include an explicit "how complex should a program be" best-practices section — complexity should be proportional to the essential behavior the program must exhibit, and a VALIDATED architectural refactor that lowers complexity (model still green under TLC/tests, behavior preserved, before/after descriptors compared) is ENCOURAGED as normal practice, not an exceptional event. Intuitions for the agent to judge with, never automated moves.
